About the Report 
We are pleased to present our second Integrated Annual Report, 
reaffirming our commitment to transparent reporting. As the 
expectations of investors, customers, and other stakeholders 
continue to evolve, we believe it is essential to provide a 
holistic view of our business, one that extends beyond financial 
performance to demonstrate how we are building resilience, 
competitiveness, and long-term value.
Reporting Period
This report covers the period from April 01, 2025 to  
March 31, 2026.
Scope and Boundary
This Integrated Report offers a perspective on our  
strategy, governance, business model, and operational 
performance, together with the risks, opportunities, and 
outcomes that are attributable to or associated with our 
key stakeholders. It goes beyond financial disclosures to include non-financial performance, and explains 
how these factors affect our ability to create, sustain, 
and share value over time, including how we are 
strengthening our business, managing resources 
responsibly, and creating impact across all capitals.
Unless otherwise specified, the information in this report 
pertains to the consolidated operations of OneSource, 
including our manufacturing plants, offices, and 
other functions.
OneSource Specialty Pharma Limited

Approach to Materiality
Material issues are identified through an ongoing and 
structured engagement process with our stakeholders, 
taking into account emerging industry trends, regulatory 
developments and key business risks.
These material topics are periodically reviewed and 
prioritised based on their potential impact on our 
strategy, operations, and long-term value creation. This 
Integrated Report outlines how these matters influence 
our performance and decision-making across the short, 
medium and long-term.
Responsibility Statement
The Board affirms that this Integrated Annual Report 
presents, in all material respects, matters that significantly 
influence our Company’s performance, strategy and 
future prospects.

=== page 19 ===
Big Picture
The global pharmaceutical landscape is evolving, driven by 
scientific progress, complex therapies, and shifting healthcare 
needs. In this environment, pharmaceutical and biotechnology 
companies are increasingly shifting to CDMOs to support 
innovation, improve operational efficiency and add flexibility to 
their supply chains. As a result, CDMOs are becoming an integral 
part of the pharmaceutical value chain.A Growing  A Growing  
Role in the Role in the 
Pharmaceutical Pharmaceutical 
IndustryIndustry
OneSource Specialty Pharma Limited
16
=== page 20 ===
Several structural trends are reshaping the pharmaceutical landscape and influencing how therapies are 
developed, manufactured, and delivered. As innovation accelerates and healthcare needs continue to evolve, 
pharmaceutical companies are rethinking supply chains, investing in complex modalities and seeking integrated 
operating models. These trends are creating new opportunities across the value chain while strengthening 
demand for specialised CDMO capabilities.
Supply Chain Diversification
The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) 2026 
and the BIOSECURE Act of the US are reshaping 
global pharmaceutical supply chains as innovators 
seek to reduce concentration risk and enhance 
supply resilience. Alongside evolving trade policies 
and supply chain diversification initiatives, these 
developments are creating long-term opportunities 
for Indian CDMOs with strong regulatory credentials, 
proven quality systems and globally compliant 
manufacturing capabilities.Biologics Tailwinds
Biologics remain one of the fastest-growing segments 
of the pharmaceutical industry, driven by expanding 
clinical applications, rising biosimilar adoption and 
a robust innovation pipeline. At the same time, 
supportive regulatory pathways are simplifying 
biosimilar development by reducing complexity, 
timelines and cost. Together, these trends are 
accelerating development programmes and increasing 
demand for CDMOs with specialised scientific 
expertise, integrated biologics capabilities and 
scalable manufacturing infrastructure.
Drug-Device Combination Momentum
DDCs are gaining traction as pharmaceutical 
companies increasingly adopt patient-centric and 
self-administered therapies. This is driving investments 
across formulation development, sterile fill-finish, 
delivery devices and specialised manufacturing 
capabilities. Patent expiries of leading GLP-1 therapies, 
including semaglutide, across more than 80 countries 
are expected to further expand opportunities in 
complex generic drug-device combinations and 
advanced drug delivery platforms.Integrated CDMO Partnerships
Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies are 
increasingly outsourcing activities, from early-stage 
development through commercialisation and lifecycle 
management. As speed-to-market and manufacturing 
readiness are becoming critical priorities, integrated 
CDMO platforms are emerging as the preferred 
delivery model. By simplifying programme 
management, reducing technology transfer risks 
and enhancing supply chain agility, these platforms 
enable a seamless transition from development to 
commercialisation while delivering greater execution 
efficiency and flexibility.
One Platform. Multiple Possibilities.
With our integrated capabilities across complex 
modalities and scalable cGMP infrastructure, we are 
strengthening our position as a trusted strategic CDMO 
partner, helping customers bring complex therapies to 
market efficiently and at scale.

quality by monitoring critical attributes 
throughout manufacturing.Specialised Softgel Expertise
Softgels require precise alignment between formulation, 
encapsulation, and downstream processing. We manage 
each of these stages, covering fill preparation, gelatin 
ribbon formation, encapsulation, drying, and inspection, 
with multiple encapsulation lines supporting production 
across formats at both development and commercial scale.
Advanced R&D Capabilities
Our development teams focus on complex oral delivery 
systems and novel formulation approaches. We have 
deep expertise in lipid-based technologies, including 
Self-Micro Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems (SMEDDS), 
helping improve bioavailability and support product 
differentiation for challenging molecules.Strong Supplier Network
We maintain supply through an established network 
of gelatin and Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC) 
suppliers, which supports flexibility, continuity of supply, 
and consistent product quality. Long-standing supplier 
relationships support operational resilience and efficient 
execution across programmes.
High-Precision Manufacturing
We run encapsulation, inspection, and packaging on 
automated systems, with high-speed contact printing 
and camera-based inspection checking that every 
capsule is correctly imprinted. Automated lubrication 
and inspection remove the manual handling points that 
cause microfractures in the capsule shell.

Our risk governance operates 
through a three-layer structure with 
defined rhythm. At the first layer, the Board, Audit Committee and 
Risk Management Committee (RMC) 
provide oversight and direction. At the 
second layer, the Steering Committee 
of the RMC reviews emerging risks, 
risk prioritisation and implementation 
of mitigation plans. At the third 
layer, designated Risk Owners drive 
monitoring of mitigation measures and 
key risk indicators.
As an example in our supply chain, 
single-source dependencies, long 
lead times and minimal buffers 
carry structural vulnerabilities, and 
in today's environment the cost of 
disruption is rarely incremental. In 
response, we have moved to resilient 
approach across our supply chain. 
This involves differentiating our 
sourcing approach between critical 
patient supply, regulated inputs and 
commodity items, strengthening 
early-warning indicators around lead 
times and quality, and deepening 
partnerships with key suppliers to 
mitigate any adverse impact. For 
a CDMO with global partners and 
patient-critical products, this is a 
matter of value protection, directly 
safeguarding earnings, cash flow and 
credibility with customers, regulators

Business Ethics
Integrity is central to how we 
operate, guiding our approach to 
fair competition, human rights and 
responsible business conduct. We 
encourage open dialogue and provide 
accessible channels for employees 
and stakeholders to safely report 
concerns or potential breaches. 
Every matter raised is reviewed and 
addressed appropriately, in line with 
our ethical standards.
Our Code of Conduct forms the basis 
of our ethics framework. It guides 
our employees and leadership in 
making decisions that align with our 
values and regulatory obligations 
and sets expectations on integrity, 
conflicts of interest, fair dealing and 
legal compliance. To further strengthen accountability, 
we have established policies and 
mechanisms, including our Anti-
Corruption and Anti-Money Laundering 
Policy and Whistleblower Policy. The 
whistleblower mechanism provides a 
secure, confidential, and transparent 
channel to report fraud, misconduct, 
or policy violations. Concerns may be 
reported anonymously, and reports 
are overseen by designated teams and 
supported by an independent third-
party administrator.

Materiality that 
Shapes our Strategy
Materiality assessment is central to how we identify the 
sustainability issues that matter most to our operations and 
stakeholders, and to how we prioritise our response to them. 
By focusing our operations on these high-priority areas, we 
strengthen stakeholder trust while embedding continuous, 
transparent dialogue across our entire value chain.
To align our approach with emerging risks and opportunities, we conducted our maiden materiality assessment 
during the year, engaging both internal and external stakeholders to identify the topics most relevant to our 
business. Our functional teams maintain ongoing dialogue with key stakeholders to build relationships, gather 
feedback, and integrate these insights into our sustainability strategy.
Stakeholders engaged in the process included Board of Directors, Executive leadership, employees, investors, 
suppliers and customers. Their inputs helped us understand which topics have the greatest impact on our business and 
where our activities create broader social and environmental impact, shaping the priorities that inform our long-term 
sustainability strategy.
Approach to Materiality
Identify Engage Analyse 
The assessment captured evolving stakeholder priorities while aligning them with our strategic objectives. We also 
established a formal review process to periodically reassess these priorities in line with changing market dynamics, 
stakeholder expectations and regulatory developments.The assessment followed a five-phase process

Product Quality Assurance 
Quality is central to our manufacturing, product stewardship and long-term value creation. Operating in a complex, 
multi-product CDMO environment, we maintain a Quality Management System (QMS) aligned with USFDA cGMP, EU GMP, 
Schedule M GMP, ICH Q10 and PIC/S standards to support consistent compliance across all manufacturing sites. 
Our QMS is built on a clearly defined Quality Framework, supported by core enablers and structured around key 
architectural pillars, reinforced by a quality culture that is proactive, responsive and committed to consistent compliance.
Our quality governance framework combines clear accountability with structured oversight across manufacturing, Quality 
Assurance, Quality Control and Technical Operations. Site-level reviews and corporate governance embed quality into 
operational decision-making at every stage. During the year, we strengthened our quality by standardising network-wide 
practices in line with evolving customer and regulatory expectations.

We implement end-to-end  
quality checks from raw material 
receipt to final product release, 
enabling early identification  
and resolution of potential issues. 
Key controls include
End-to-End Quality Checks:  
Stringent inspections are 
implemented at every stage of the 
production cycle from raw material 
receipt to final product testing to 
detect and eliminate defects early.
Qualified Vendors:  Raw materials, 
excipients, and critical consumables 
are sourced only from qualified 
suppliers. Vendors undergo periodic 
requalification to confirm the 
robustness of their Quality Systems 
and continued compliance with 
regulatory requirements.
SOP-Governed Operations:  All 
manufacturing and testing activities 
follow well-defined Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) to 
ensure consistency, accuracy, and 
reduced risk of human error.
100% Visual Inspection: 
Regardless of dosage form (powder, 
lyophilised, suspension, liquid, pre-
filled syringe, or cartridge), every 
product is subjected to 100% visual 
inspection before final packing.
Validated Packaging and 
Transport: Packing configuration, 
orientation, and transport validation 
are thoroughly performed to 
maintain product integrity and 
prevent delivery of defective items.
Together, these measures 
fortify our quality-by-design 
manufacturing approach.

Biosimilar Peptide Pen
CHALLENGE
A biosimilar peptide programme required a patient-friendly reusable pen for elderly users with limited 
dexterity. The programme involved device selection, drug-cartridge compatibility and compliance with EU 
MDR requirements.
ONESOURCE APPROACH
Leveraged a proprietary pen platform, assessed drug-device and drug-cartridge interface compatibility, 
conducted cartridge extractables and leachables (E&L) studies, and completed dose-use validation across 
temperature and humidity conditions. Supported the programme through design verification (DV), human factors 
studies (HFS) and EU CE notified-body certification.CASE STUDY: DRUG-DEVICE INTEGRATION

Intellectual Property Governance 
Our Commitment 
Intellectual Property (IP) is 
fundamental to pharmaceutical 
innovation and our customers’ 
competitive advantage. We 
manage these assets through a 
robust governance framework 
designed to protect proprietary 
information, enable secure 
collaboration and support seamless 
technology transfers. 
This approach safeguards 
customer innovations, supports 
regulatory compliance, and 
enables responsible knowledge 
sharing throughout the product 
lifecycle. This commitment is 
formalised through our IP Policy and 
extends across the organisation. 
All our employees, contractors, 
consultants, and approved 
subcontractors are required to 
comply with its provisions in relation 
to both physical and digital assets, 
including those managed through 
our integrated technology platforms.
Our IP Policy
Our IP Policy provides a clear framework for managing intellectual property 
across the full lifecycle of customer engagements, from development through 
commercial manufacturing. It distinguishes between customer-owned IP, 
OneSource’s independently developed IP, and project-specific IP generated 
during an engagement, with ownership and usage rights defined through 
contractual arrangements.
Key aspects of the policy include:
Robust frameworks  governing the ownership, protection, and use 
of customer IP, OneSource proprietary technologies, and project-
specific intellectual property
Confidentiality and access controls  based on need-to-know 
principles and secure systems
Protection of proprietary information  across both physical and 
digital assets
Guidance on responsible use and transfer of IP during 
collaboration and technology transfer
Support for regulatory compliance  and secure handling of 
technical and product-related information
Defined internal roles and accountability for effective 
implementation and oversight

Framework for IP Ownership and Rights 
Respecting Customer Ownership
All proprietary information provided by a customer, including formulations, cell lines, sequences, specifications, 
regulatory dossiers, among others, remain the property of the customer. These are used solely to deliver the contracted 
services. No such customer assets may be reused, redirected, disclosed or exploited for any purpose other than 
fulfilment of the applicable engagement.
Innovation generated during our partnerships follows clear, equitable allocation principles tailored to asset 
protection and commercial agility
Customer IP
IP developed during a 
programme that relates directly 
to a customer’s product or 
process is assigned to the 
customer on completion of 
payment obligations. This 
includes batch records, reports, 
analytics, among others, 
ensuring customer retains full 
control over innovations tied to 
their commercial assets.OneSource Platform IP
OneSource Platform IP 
developed independently 
without use of client confidential 
information, remains 
OneSource property. This 
includes platform methods, 
manufacturing heuristics and 
software tools that enhance 
our service capabilities across 
multiple clients. Collaborative Innovation
Where both parties contribute, 
ownership is defined within 
the project scope, with default 
provisions favouring customer 
ownership while retaining 
our ability to serve the wider 
industry without creating 
competitive conflicts.

covenant not to assert IP developed 
for a customer against that customer, 
its affiliates, authorised licensees, or

Product Stewardship
Stewardship by Design:  We integrate 
quality, safety and manufacturability 
from the earliest stages using quality-
by-design principles, advanced 
formulation expertise and end-
to-end development capabilities. 
Seamless analytical method transfer, 
from process development to cGMP 
manufacturing, ensures efficient 
technology transfer and reliable 
regulatory outcomes.
Environmental Stewardship: We 
embed environmental responsibility 
across our manufacturing processes 
through an ISO 14001:2015-certified 
Environmental Management 
System. During the year, we sourced 
approximately 81% of our energy 
from renewable sources and maintained Zero Liquid Discharge 
systems across our manufacturing 
facilities. We advanced sustainable 
manufacturing practices aimed at 
enhancing resource efficiency and 
reducing the environmental footprint 
of our operations.
Responsible Hazard Management:  
We adopt responsible manufacturing 
practices to minimise waste, 
optimise resource utilisation, and 
support environmental performance 
across our operations. During FY26, 
hazardous waste intensity stood at 
0.019 MT per ₹ million of revenue. 
All manufacturing and R&D sites 
are compliant with applicable 
environmental laws, and none are 
located in ecologically sensitive areas. Beyond managing hazardous 
waste, we systematically assess the 
intrinsic health-hazard and exposure 
profile of every pharmaceutical 
substance we handle. As a pharma 
CDMO, we recognise our responsibility 
to ensure the safe handling of the 
pharmaceutical compounds entrusted 
to us. While product ownership 
resides with our customers, we 
maintain robust systems to identify, 
assess, and manage occupational 
health, safety and environmental risks 
associated with materials handled 
across our operations. Every molecule 
entering our facilities undergoes 
a structured toxicological and 
occupational health risk assessment 
conducted by qualified, independent 
Certified Industrial Hygienists, We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of product quality, safety, and compliance across our 
development and manufacturing activities. Supported by robust quality systems, risk-based oversight, and continuous 
monitoring, we help ensure the consistent delivery of safe, effective, and high-quality pharmaceutical products.

following an internationally 
recognised methodology aligned with 
the International Council of Chemical 
Associations (ICCA) four-step 
framework: hazard identification, 
hazard characterisation, 
exposure assessment, and 
risk characterisation.
These assessments establish 
substance-specific control 
parameters before manufacturing 
begins. For instance, our occupational 
risk assessment of a product derived 
a protective Occupational Exposure 
Limit (OEL) of 70 µg/m³ (Occupational 
Exposure Band OEB-3), incorporating 
a conservative severity factor 
for its anticoagulant effects. The 
substance was confirmed to be non-
carcinogenic and non-mutagenic, 
with no teratogenic or reproductive 
effects in available studies. Such 
limits directly inform task-level 
workplace risk assessments and 
the design of engineering and 
administrative controls that protect 
our workforce.
Importantly, the pharmaceutical APIs 
and medicinal products we process 
are not classified as Persistent 
Organic Pollutants (POPs) under 
the Stockholm Convention/EU POP 
Regulation, nor as Substances of Very 
High Concern (SVHC) or restricted 
substances under EU REACH. Our 
exposure to regulated hazardous 
industrial chemicals is therefore not 
material, while residual occupational 
risk from pharmacologically potent 
compounds is proactively managed 
through science-led exposure limits 
and rigorous handling protocols.
Lifecycle Stewardship:  Our approach 
extends beyond manufacturing 
to include lifecycle management, 
regulatory submission support and 
continuous improvement. Supported 
by structured quality governance 
and regular management reviews, 
we maintain product safety, supply 
reliability and regulatory compliance 
throughout the commercial lifecycle.Intellectual Capital
Driving Process Innovation by 
Integrating Green Chemistry Principles 
During the year, we initiated Life 
Cycle Assessments (LCAs) for select 
products, to better understand 
and quantify the environmental 
impacts associated with their 
production across the value chain. 
The assessments covered cradle-
to-gate stages and evaluated 
lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions 
to identify environmental hotspots 
and opportunities for mitigation. The 
scope of the assessments included 
a broad range of impact categories 
such as global warming potential, 
stratospheric ozone depletion, 
terrestrial acidification, freshwater 
and marine eutrophication, human 
toxicity, terrestrial and aquatic ecotoxicity, ozone formation, ionising 
radiation, particulate matter, land 
use, among others. 
Insights generated through these 
assessments will support future 
process optimisation, resource 
efficiency initiatives and the 
integration of environmental 
considerations into product and 
process decision-making.
This integrated stewardship 
framework translates our scientific 
expertise into commercial 
reliability, regulatory confidence 
and sustainable value for customers 
and patients.
Green chemistry remains integral 
to our approach to responsible 
manufacturing. Through efficient 
process design, waste minimisation, 
and prudent resource utilisation, we 
seek to reduce our environmental 
footprint while enhancing 
operational efficiency.
Building on established practices, 
we continue to strengthen these 
principles across our operations 
through process optimisation, 
source-level waste segregation and 
the application of the 3R framework 
(Reduce, Reuse, Recycle). As one 
of the few CDMOs with integrated microbial and mammalian biologics 
capabilities, we are guided by 
green chemistry principles in the 
development and manufacture of 
advanced therapeutics. For instance, 
our E. coli-based insulin production 
process is designed to deliver high 
yields through efficient and scalable 
manufacturing. These principles are 
further reflected in our environmental 
management practices, including 
the responsible treatment of process 
effluents, controlled inactivation of 
biological materials prior to disposal, 
and the use of engineered safeguards 
for the handling of biological waste 
and hazardous substances.

confidential customer information, 
including proprietary formulations, 
manufacturing processes, analytical

among others. Protecting 
these assets is fundamental 
to maintaining customer trust, 
supporting regulatory compliance, 
and safeguarding intellectual

through a structured framework, 
rooted in transparency, security, 
confidentiality and consent.Protecting Customer Data 
We maintain a robust data 
governance framework built on

that data is accessed only by

Responsible Artificial Intelligence
Governance and Controls 
As artificial intelligence becomes 
increasingly integrated into 
pharmaceutical manufacturing 
and development, we are focused 
on adopting AI responsibly to 
enhance scientific, operational, 
and business capabilities. Our 
AI governance framework is 
designed to ensure that AI-enabled 
solutions operate in alignment 
with regulatory requirements, data 
protection obligations, and internal 
control standards.
Potential risks associated with AI, 
including model inaccuracies, data 
quality issues, and inappropriate 
use, are managed through defined 
governance processes, risk 
assessments, validation protocols, 
and ongoing oversight. Higher-
risk applications are subject to 
enhanced review and monitoring 
to ensure operational integrity and 
regulatory compliance. Policy and Oversight
Our Responsible AI Policy establishes 
the principles governing the 
development, deployment, and 
use of AI across the organisation. 
The policy emphasises responsible 
innovation and sets clear expectations 
around accountability, transparency, 
data privacy, cybersecurity, and 
appropriate human oversight. We 
deploy AI-enabled solutions in 
accordance with applicable regulatory 
requirements and internal governance 
standards, with individuals remaining 
accountable for decisions supported 
by AI-generated outputs. The policy 
further establishes governance 
requirements and control mechanisms 
to help ensure that AI technologies 
are used securely, ethically and in 
accordance with applicable regulatory 
and internal standards. Data Stewardship 
As digital tools and artificial 
intelligence become increasingly 
embedded across the pharmaceutical 
value chain, we maintain robust 
standards for the protection and 
responsible use of data. Customer 
information is used only for 
authorised business purposes 
and managed in accordance with 
contractual, regulatory, and privacy 
requirements.
We are committed to safeguarding 
customer confidentiality and 
ensuring that the use of data for 
analytics, automation, and process 
improvement is governed by 
appropriate controls, transparency, 
and data protection principles. This 
approach reinforces customer trust 
while enabling responsible digital 
innovation across the organisation.
People remain the first line of defence 
against evolving cyber threats. We 
recognise that strong cybersecurity 
is not only a technology priority but 
also a shared responsibility across 
the organisation. Through structured 
training programmes, onboarding 
initiatives and regular awareness 
campaigns, we equip employees 
with the knowledge and confidence 
to identify, mitigate and promptly 
escalate potential cyber threats.
Cybersecurity and information 
security training form an integral 
part of our employee onboarding 
process, establishing a strong 
foundation in responsible technology 
usage, data protection, secure 
handling of information and incident Cybersecurity Training and Awareness 
reporting protocols. Employees are 
introduced to key security principles 
and expected behaviours from the 
outset, helping embed cybersecurity 
awareness into everyday work 
practices.
Our ongoing awareness programme 
reinforces this foundation through 
weekly communications, targeted

emerging cyber threats, evolving

We also encourage a culture of

Performance Evaluation
We follow a structured performance management 
system designed to drive accountability, recognise 
merit and support individual development.  At the 
beginning of each performance cycle, employees 
and managers jointly establish SMART goals aligned 
with individual roles, functional priorities, and 
organisational objectives. Progress against these 
goals is reviewed throughout the year and forms the 
foundation of the year-end performance evaluation, 
fostering objective performance measurement. 
For mid and senior management, performance 
assessment is strengthened through structured 
calibration. Ratings are reviewed in facilitated sessions 
with functional heads and business leadership, 
supported by performance trend data and year-on-
year comparatives, to ensure consistency of standards 
across functions and sites and to reduce individual 
manager bias in the final outcome.We promote continuous performance management 
through regular manager-employee interactions rather 
than relying solely on an annual appraisal. Employees 
participate in periodic performance discussions, 
including monthly connects and quarterly performance 
reviews, to track progress, deliver timely feedback and 
enable course correction where required.
Individual evaluations are complemented by 
organisational performance considerations. While 
employees are assessed against individual goals, final 
outcomes also reflect collective business performance. 
Corporate employees are evaluated with reference 
to organisational performance, while manufacturing 
personnel are aligned with unit-level outcomes, 
reinforcing shared accountability. 01

and confidential grievance and 
escalation channels through which

Human Capital
The safety of our people is 
fundamental to our operational 
sustainability. We are proud to report 
a zero-fatality  rate across both 
employees and contractors for the 
fourth consecutive financial year, 
including FY26.
During the year under review, we also 
recorded zero work-related injuries or 
high-consequence incidents, resulting 
in a Lost Time Injury Frequency 
Rate (LTIFR) of zero, demonstrating 
the efficacy of our workplace 
safety protocols. 
Our approach to workplace safety 
begins with rigorous hazard 
identification and risk assessment. 
In line with our ISO 45001:2018 
certification, we follow a robust 
risk management and prevention 
framework based on Aspect Impact 
Management (AIM) and have a well-
established Hazard Identification and 
Risk Assessment (HIRA) procedure 
covering all processes, including 
chemical handling, equipment 
operation, and laboratory activities.Through this process, hazards are 
comprehensively identified, risks are 
evaluated based on likelihood and 
severity and mitigation strategies 
with quantified targets are developed 
for all identified hazards. These 
assessments are regularly reviewed 
and updated to reflect changes in 
operations or the work environment, 
ensuring continuous progress towards 
reducing health and safety risks.
Regular audits and inspections form a 
critical pillar of our OHS management 
system. Routine internal inspections 
are conducted across all sites to 
verify compliance, identify potential 
hazards and confirm the effective 
implementation of corrective actions. 
Independent third-party audits in 
accordance with ISO 45001:2018 
provide objective assessment and 
identify improvement opportunities. 
Complementing these efforts, we 
conduct safety committee meetings 
at regular intervals to review OHS 
performance and analyse incident 
trends, bringing together management 
and worker representatives to ensure collaborative decision-making. We 
believe that employees closest to day-
to-day operations play a critical role in 
identifying hazards, improving safety 
practices, and fostering a culture 
of shared responsibility. Worker 
participation is therefore embedded 
in our safety committee structure, 
incident investigations and the 
development of safety procedures, 
reinforcing a culture of shared 
responsibility across the organisation.
To sustain this culture, all new 
employees and on-site contractors 
receive mandatory onboarding 
training, covering hazard identification, 
safe work practices and reporting 
protocols, supplemented by periodic 
refresher courses. Training is delivered 
through multiple channels, including 
our Electronic Document Management 
System (EDMS) for digital learning, 
structured classroom sessions and 
regular Toolbox Talks at the worksite. 
Behavioural safety programmes 
and awareness campaigns further 
promote proactive safety behaviour 
and encourage the reporting of 
unsafe practices. Training compliance 
is monitored across all sites, and 
records are maintained as part of our 
management system documentation. 
We further strengthened safety 
awareness through targeted 
engagement and preparedness 
initiatives during the year. The 
55th National Safety Week was 
observed from March 09 to March 
16, 2026 through a range of 
awareness activities promoting safe 
workplace practices. A Safety Mela 
was organised for employees and 
contractors, encouraging active 
participation in safety-focused 
programmes and reinforcing a culture 
of shared responsibility. People Safety

We will continue strengthening the people, leadership, and culture that support organisational excellence and 
long-term competitiveness. Our focus will remain on building critical capabilities, developing future leaders, 
and creating meaningful growth opportunities for employees across the organisation. 
By fostering a culture of performance, safety, inclusion, and accountability, we seek to build a resilient

On the ground, Personal Protective 
Equipment (PPE) usage is strictly 
enforced, with employees trained on 
proper selection, use, maintenance 
and disposal of respiratory masks,

comprehensive occupational health 
services to protect and monitor 
workforce well-being. These include 
pre-employment medical check-ups 
to establish baseline health status, 
half-yearly check-ups for workers in 
high-risk areas and annual check-ups 
for all workers to track health trends 
and detect work-related impacts early. 
Our dedicated Occupational Health 
Centre (OHC), led by qualified medical 
personnel, provides immediate care, 
health surveillance and well-being 
support. The OHC is accessible to 
all workers, including contractors 
and third-party personnel, ensuring 
equitable access regardless of 
employment status. Specialised 
programmes focusing on stress 
management and mental well-being 
are also available to all employees. Our Emergency 
Action Plan 
We maintain a comprehensive 
emergency preparedness framework 
covering fire, chemical spills, medical 
emergencies and natural disasters, 
with defined roles, communication 
protocols and evacuation strategies. 
Regular mock drills and simulations 
for employees, contractors and 
third-party workers, followed by 
debriefs, help identify gaps and drive 
improvements. Sites are equipped 
with fire detection and suppression 
systems, spill containment equipment, 
first aid stations and trained 
first responders.

Environment, Health, and Safety Governance Practice
Our approach to Environment, Health 
and Safety (EHS) governance is 
guided by our Environment, Health 
and Safety Policy & Framework 
and Sustainability Policy. Together, 
they define our commitment to 
minimising environmental impact, 
ensuring regulatory compliance and 
driving continuous improvement 
across operations.
Oversight of environmental and 
sustainability -related matters 
is provided by the Board of 
Directors through the Board-level 
Environmental, Social and 
Governance (ESG) Committee. The 
ESG Committee is responsible for 
reviewing, monitoring compliance 
and overseeing the implementation of 
sustainability priorities. Environmental 
performance, risks and improvement 
initiatives are reviewed periodically 
and reported to the Board.
Operational responsibility for EHS 
governance is embedded across 
the organisation through clearly 
defined roles and accountability 
mechanisms. Senior management sets strategic direction and ensures 
alignment of environmental 
priorities with medium and long-
term business objectives. The EHS 
Head is responsible for establishing 
environmental management systems, 
monitoring performance, conducting 
internal audits and facilitating 
compliance across all manufacturing 
locations. Site -level governance 
is led by site leadership and EHS 
teams, who are responsible for 
effective implementation of policies, 
standard operating procedures and 
regulatory requirements.
All of our manufacturing units are 
certified to ISO 14001 and ISO 
45001, reflecting a structured 
approach to managing environmental 
and occupational health and safety 
risks. Compliance is monitored 
through internal audits as well as 
periodic external audits conducted by 
accredited certification bodies. 
In accordance with applicable 
regulatory requirements, we submit 
half-yearly Environmental Clearance 
(EC) compliance reports to the Ministry of Environment, Forest 
and Climate Change (MoEFCC) for 
applicable sites, while maintaining 
transparent engagement with all 
the regulators. 
During the year, no material penalties 
or fines were imposed by regulatory 
authorities for environmental or 
safety -related non -compliance.
Environmental Compliance 
and Risk Management
We assess environmental risks, 
including those related to energy, 
water availability, pollution, regulatory 
compliance, and climate, as part of 
our ERM framework. These risks are 
reviewed periodically to evaluate 
their potential impact on operations 
and identify appropriate mitigation 
measures. Through established 
management systems, regular 
monitoring and proactive risk 
management practices, we seek to 
strengthen operational resilience 
and maintain high standards of 
environmental compliance.Natural Capital

Energy Management and GHG emissions
We follow a structured approach 
focused on improving efficiency, 
optimising resource use and reducing 
emissions intensity.
Energy consumption and greenhouse 
gas emissions are key considerations 
for our manufacturing operations.
In FY26, total electricity consumption 
stood at 1,40,062.83 GJ, with 
1,13,219.09 GJ sourced from 
renewable energy, accounting for 
approximately 81% of our total 
electricity, secured through power 
purchase agreements. 
Process and technology improvements 
in water and wastewater systems 
contributed to energy efficiency:
• Installation of high -efficiency 
oxy-rich diffuser systems in effluent 
treatment plants, improving 
aeration efficiency and reducing 
power consumption
• Adoption of advanced membrane 
technologies in ZLD systems, 
enabling higher recovery with lower 
energy use per unit of water treated
• Deployment of Membrane 
Bioreactor (MBR) systems, 
increasing treatment capacity 
within the same footprint and 
improving operational efficiency
• Increased reuse of treated water 
in utilities (~220 KL/day), lowering 
energy requirements associated 
with freshwater extraction 
and handling
During the year, we conducted a 
comprehensive energy audit at our 
flagship site in collaboration with 
an independent energy consultant. The assessment covered key 
energy-intensive systems, including 
HVAC infrastructure, chillers, air 
handling units, compressed air 
systems, transformers, utilities and 
wastewater treatment operations. 
The audit identified multiple energy 
conservation opportunities focused on 
optimising equipment performance, 
reducing utility losses and improving 
operational efficiency. 
These initiatives support our broader 
efforts to reduce our carbon footprint. 
We monitor Scope 1, Scope 2 and 
Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions 
in line with the Greenhouse Gas 
Protocol. Emissions data is tracked 
for internal review and disclosed 
transparently, alongside intensity 
metrics, to support decision -making 
and continuous improvement. In 
FY26, our combined Scope 1 and 
Scope 2 emissions were 14,836.46 
MtCO₂e and Scope 3 emissions were 
74,414.37 MtCO₂e. 
We remain committed to a progressive 
reduction in Scope 1 and Scope 2 
emissions. To this effect, we have 
articulated a medium -term ambition 
to transition towards 100% renewable 
energy for our operations.Climate Risk 
Management
Climate change is an increasingly 
important consideration for the 
pharmaceutical manufacturing 
sector, with the potential to influence 
operations, supply chains, resource 
availability, infrastructure resilience, 
and stakeholder expectations. As a 
specialty pharmaceutical CDMO serving

a complex supply chain, we recognise 
the importance of strengthening 
resilience to climate-related risks 
while identifying opportunities

To strengthen our preparedness, we 
are progressively integrating climate-
related considerations into our

and strategic planning processes. 
During the year, we initiated a climate 
risk assessment to evaluate potential 
climate-related impacts across our 
operations and value chain. The 
assessment considered both physical 
risks, including heat stress, water 
availability constraints and extreme 
weather events, as well as transition 
risks arising from evolving regulations, 
technological developments and 
changing market expectations.

Water Management
Water is a critical resource for 
pharmaceutical manufacturing and 
a priority area in our environmental 
management approach. We 
adopt comprehensive water 
stewardship practices focused on 
conservation, efficiency, reuse and 
responsible discharge.
In FY26, our total water consumption 
stood at 2,55,733.71 KL. Water 
consumption is monitored across 
key process points using flow 
meters and smart metering systems, 
enabling real -time visibility and 
control. We also track specific water 
consumption year -on-year to drive 
continuous improvement.
During the year, we implemented 
a combination of process 
enhancements and infrastructure 
interventions to optimise water use:• Deployment of advanced ZLD 
systems with high efficiency RO 
at our flagship site, facilitating the 
reuse of ~220 KL/day in boilers and 
cooling towers 
• Segregation of low TDS streams 
(purified water and WFI rejects) 
at the R&D unit in Bengaluru, 
enabling reuse in fire water systems 
and gardening, resulting in ~20 
KL/month freshwater reduction 
while eliminating associated 
treatment costs 
• Installation of auto sensor fixtures, 
auto level controllers and improved 
fittings to minimise losses and 
prevent overflows 
• Strengthened leak 
detection through sensors, 
preventive maintenance and 
pipeline inspections 
• Internal water audits, 
benchmarking and real-time 
monitoring through smart meters
Our wastewater management 
practices are aligned with stringent 
environmental standards, and 
all our manufacturing facilities 
operate ZLD systems. During FY26, 
a comprehensive environmental 
audit at flagship site reviewed 
water withdrawal, wastewater 
treatment, recycling and reuse 
systems, treated effluent quality and 
site-level conservation measures. 
The assessment highlighted the site’s continued focus on resource 
efficiency through the reuse of 
treated wastewater across utility 
and process application, identifying 
opportunities to deploy advanced 
membrane systems to improve the 
recovery and quality of recycled water 
in ZLD operations.
We further strengthened water 
recycling and treatment performance 
through deployment of advanced 
technologies, including Membrane 
Bioreactor (MBR) systems, high-
efficiency oxy-rich diffusers, advanced 
membrane-based recovery systems 
and high-efficiency softeners. These 
interventions improve water quality 
and increase reuse opportunities 
across operations.
To reduce dependence on freshwater 
sources, rainwater harvesting systems 
are operational across facilities. At 
flagship site, a dedicated pond with 
a capacity of 1,500 KL supported 
the harvesting of approximately 
9,000 KL of rainwater during the year.
The facility also directs stormwater 
runoff to groundwater recharge pits, 
supporting aquifer replenishment 
and strengthening local water 
stewardship. In parallel, employee 
awareness programmes reinforce 
responsible water use and timely 
reporting of inefficiencies, supporting 
a culture of conservation across 
our operations.
The assessment framework evaluates 
acute and chronic physical hazards, 
including flooding, heat stress, drought 
and other extreme weather events, 
alongside transition risks associated 
with policy developments, technology 
shifts, market dynamics and the 
global transition towards a lower-
carbon economy. The exercise also 
supports identification of opportunities 
related to resource efficiency, 
renewable energy adoption, low-
carbon technologies and enhanced 
operational resilience.
Through this ongoing effort, we 
aim to strengthen organisational 
preparedness, enhance climate 
resilience and support informed 
decision-making across our operations. 
As our sustainability journey continues 
to evolve, we remain committed to 
integrating climate considerations into 
our business processes and reinforcing 
our approach to sustainable and 
resilient growth.

Natural Capital
Waste Management
Responsible waste management 
is integral to our sustainability 
commitments and operational 
practices. We aim to minimise 
waste generation at source and 
embed circularity principles across 
our processes, guided by the 3R 
framework (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) 
and the principles of green chemistry. 
Our processes are designed to ensure 
that input materials, operations and 
outputs are managed efficiently, 
reducing environmental impact across 
the value chain. During FY26, our 
operations generated 838.11 MT of 
waste, comprising both hazardous 
and non-hazardous streams. Of this, 
541.69 MT were recovered through 
recycling and reuse, reflecting our 
commitment to resource efficiency. 
The remaining waste was managed 
through authorised third-party 
handlers, with 260.04 MT incinerated 
and 36.38 MT landfilled, in 
compliance with regulatory norms.Our waste handling governance 
extends beyond our facilities to 
include third-party partners. All 
vendors undergo stringent EHS 
screening, risk assessments and 
periodic audits to ensure adherence 
to contractual and legislative 
requirements. Waste streams such as 
plastic, biomedical and electronics 
are routed to authorised recyclers or 
incineration agencies approved by 
the Karnataka State Pollution Control 
Board (KSPCB). As an importer 
under the Producer, Importer, and 
Brand Owner (PIBO) category, we 
have obtained Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) registration and 
submit annual returns to the Central 
Pollution Control Board, ensuring 
compliance with Extended Producer 
Responsibility norms.
In FY26, an environmental audit 
at our flagship site reviewed 
hazardous and non-hazardous waste 
management practices, including segregation, storage, handling, 
recycling and disposal arrangements. 
The assessment reaffirmed the 
effectiveness of existing waste 
management controls and identified 
opportunities for further strengthening 
resource recovery practices.
Employee awareness programmes, 
promotion of alternatives to single-use 
plastics and systematic segregation 
at source further strengthen our 
waste management efforts. Internal 
assessments confirm that our 
operations have no significant actual 
or potential waste-related impacts, 
yet we continue to explore circular 
economy practices and reduce landfill 
dependency. Looking ahead, we aim 
to strengthen recovery systems, 
deepen supplier engagement and 
adopt innovative solutions to improve 
diversion rates and long-term 
waste sustainability.
Biodiversity
To support and protect biodiversity 
around our manufacturing sites, we 
have formalised our conservation 
efforts through a Biodiversity 
Commitment Statement. The 
statement defines our governance 
approach, key responsibilities and 
long-term objectives, including 
measures to support biodiversity 
conservation and avoid deforestation.
To minimise our environmental 
footprint, we have developed 
biodiversity roadmap aligned with 
local ecological conditions and 
implemented site-specific mitigation 
measures. During the year, we 
initiated ecological surveys and impact 
assessments in areas surrounding 
select manufacturing facilities to 
better understand baseline conditions, 
potential risks and opportunities for 
ecological enhancement.Based on these assessments, we are 
undertaking targeted mitigation and 
restoration initiatives. At our flagship 
site, located near a lake managed 
by Karnataka Industrial Areas 
Development Board (KIADB), we 
have initiated a biodiversity impact 
analysis and rejuvenation programme 
for the adjoining water body.  The initiative aims to support 
ecosystem restoration, improve 
local habitat conditions and 
enhance long -term environmental 
value. As part of this programme, 
OneSource has committed to 
planting approximately 5,000 native 
and adaptive tree species by 2027, 
strengthening green cover.

Life Cycle Assessment
As part of our efforts to strengthen sustainable manufacturing practices and enhance our understanding of 
environmental impacts across the value chain, we have conducted a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) during the year 
for select products. The assessment evaluated environmental impacts across major stages of product lifecycle, 
including raw material sourcing, transportation, manufacturing and packaging.
The study provided insights into resource consumption and environmental impacts across the value chain, helping 
identify opportunities to further improve operational efficiency, sustainable sourcing, resource management and 
packaging practices. The findings will support future decision-making as we continue to integrate sustainability 
considerations into our operations and product stewardship approach.
Way Forward
We will continue to strengthen our environmental performance through responsible resource management 
and operational efficiency. Our focus will remain on advancing renewable energy adoption, enhancing water 
stewardship, improving waste circularity, and integrating climate resilience into our operations. 
We will also continue to support biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration initiatives while 
embedding environmental considerations into decision-making across the business. Through these efforts, we 
seek to reduce our environmental footprint and support sustainable, resilient operations.

Risk Management
Building Resilience 
through Risk Management 
Our business operates in a complex, highly regulated 
environment shaped by evolving customer expectations, 
global supply chain dependencies and shifting geopolitical 
dynamics. Risk management is embedded across our 
planning, operations, and decision-making, helping us 
anticipate disruptions and safeguard business continuity.

Risk Oversight through the Risk 
Management Committee (RMC)Risk Management – At a Glance
We view risk management as a strategic enabler that informs capital allocation, strengthens investment 
decisions, safeguards product quality and patient trust and drives sustainable growth. Our Enterprise Risk 
Management (ERM) framework follows the principles of the Committee of Sponsoring Organisations of the 
Treadway Commission (COSO), and is applied across all functions and business units.
OneSource Specialty Pharma Limited 116
=== page 120 ===
Governance, Oversight, and Risk Culture
Board of Directors 
The Board of Directors retains ultimate accountability for our risk management framework.  
It reviews and approves the overall risk approach, ensuring alignment between the organisation’s risk  
posture and its strategic objectives. 
Risk Management Committee 
The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee, which meets semi-annually to review the enterprise 
risk landscape, assess the effectiveness of mitigation measures, and evaluate the implications of significant 
changes in the internal and external operating environment.
Management Steering Committee 
Assists the RMC in evaluating key risks and the 
effectiveness of controls. It comprises the CFO, 
who is Acting Chief Risk Officer, together with the 
Chief Quality Officer, Chief Operating Officer, and 
Chief Business Officer.
The Steering Committee operationalises our ERM 
framework, driving risk identification, prioritisation 
and mitigation across business units. It monitors 
Key Risk Indicators (KRI), consolidates enterprise 
risk positions and coordinates cross-functional 
responses to material risks, including ESG 
considerations. Through periodic reporting to the 
Risk Management Committee and implementation 
of Board directives, it helps align operational 
risk management with strategic governance and 
embed ESG considerations into decision-making.Dedicated Risk Owners
Senior leaders act as risk champions for specific risk 
themes, cascading ownership and accountability 
through their departments and functions. They 
provide monthly updates on mitigation progress and 
KRI performance to the Steering Committee. This 
distributed model ensures that risk management 
is embedded in day-to-day decision-making and 
that accountability is shared across all levels of 
the organisation.Effective risk management begins 
with strong governance and a 
culture of accountability. Oversight 
is anchored at the Board level 
and cascades through a layered 
governance structure so that risks are 
identified, owned, and monitored at 
the appropriate level. 
Our Risk Management Policy provides 
the foundational framework for 
identifying, evaluating, mitigating, and monitoring risks across the 
organisation, covering financial, 
operational, sectoral, ESG, information 
security, and cyber security risks, 
ensuring a holistic and integrated 
approach. The policy defines clear 
processes for risk identification, 
control design, mitigation planning, 
and ongoing monitoring. It is reviewed 
periodically to remain responsive to 
changes in the external environment, 
industry dynamics, and the growing complexity of our operations. Any 
material amendments to the policy 
require Board approval, and the Board 
is kept informed of key developments, 
recommendations, and actions arising 
from risk management discussions.
These governance mechanisms are reinforced by regular training, continuous monitoring, and clear accountability 
frameworks that help cultivate a proactive and risk-aware culture across the organisation.

Risk Management
We operate a comprehensive Three 
Lines of Defence risk management 
model to ensure our risk-related 
objectives are achieved. The Board, 
supported by the Board Risk 
Management Committee , provides 
overall oversight of the enterprise 
risk management framework and 
approves the organisation’s risk 
appetite, ensuring that key risks are 
identified, assessed, and managed in 
line with strategic objectives. First-
line business and process owners 
are responsible for managing risks 
Our ERM framework provides a structured and repeatable process for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and 
monitoring risks across the enterprise. It covers strategic, operational, financial, and compliance-related risks 
and is integrated into our governance, planning and decision-making processes.and maintaining effective controls 
within their day-to-day operations and 
decision-making activities.
The ERM Function, led and 
coordinated by the Acting Chief 
Risk Officer , along with specialist 
functions such as Quality, 
Compliance, Information Security, 
and Environment, Health and Safety 
(EHS), delivers second-line support 
through risk expertise, policy 
guidance, independent monitoring, 
and constructive challenge. Internal Audit serves as the 
independent third line of defence , 
providing objective assurance on the 
effectiveness of governance, risk 
management, and internal control 
processes to the Audit Committee and 
the Board. 
This integrated approach ensures 
clear accountability, comprehensive 
risk identification and assessment, 
and continuous improvement of our 
risk management practices across 
all functions and business units.

Global Economic Review
According to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) 
World Economic Outlook released in April 2026, the global 
economy is going through a fragile and uneven recovery, 
growing more slowly than its long-term average as it deals 
with a more uncertain environment. Global growth is 
projected at 3.1% in 2026 before improving marginally to 
3.2% in 2027, reflecting geopolitical tensions, evolving trade 
policies, tighter financial conditions, and slowing momentum 
across several major economies. While economic activity 
remains positive, growth is expected to remain below Management Discussion & Analysis
historical averages, highlighting the challenges associated 
with an increasingly complex global landscape.
Growth is increasingly uneven across countries. Advanced 
economies are expected to slow gradually, as the delayed 
effects of higher interest rates continue to weigh on spending, 
investment and industrial output. Higher borrowing costs, 
fiscal pressures, and weaker productivity are expected to 
hold back growth across several developed markets.
Emerging and developing economies remain a key driver of 
global growth, expanding at 3.9% in 2026 and 4.2% in 2027 
according to the IMF, supported by favourable demographics, 
urbanisation, infrastructure investment, and rising domestic 
spending. Asia remains a key growth engine whereas several 
emerging markets are benefiting as supply chains diversify 
and companies invest in new industrial capacity. However, 
the growth is uneven and dependent on external financing 
conditions, currency movements, commodity prices, and 
varying levels of exposure to global demand.
The conflict in the Middle East, which began in late February 
2026 and led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and 
damage to major oil production facilities, has been a key 
factor behind this year’s global growth outlook, driving up 
oil and commodity prices, raising transportation costs, 
and creating risks to global supply chains. The size of the 
shock to the global economy will depend on how long the 
conflict lasts, how widely it spreads, and how quickly energy 
production and transit can return to normal once hostilities 
end.
At the same time, global trade is being reshaped by rising 
protectionism and strategic economic competition. Recent 
US tariff measures, and the risk of further trade restrictions, 
are pushing companies to reassess where they source, 
manufacture and ship from, accelerating a shift toward 
regional supply chains and new manufacturing hubs in 
emerging markets.Company Profile
OneSource Specialty Pharma Limited (OneSource) is a pure-play specialty pharmaceutical Contract Development and 
Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO) providing integrated development and manufacturing solutions across complex 
pharmaceutical modalities. We partner with leading global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across the product 
lifecycle, from early-stage development through commercialisation and lifecycle management, leveraging deep scientific 
expertise, advanced manufacturing capabilities and a strong regulatory compliance framework.
We operate a differentiated, multi-modality CDMO platform spanning drug-device combinations (including GLP-1 therapies), 
biologics, sterile fill-finish and oral technologies (soft gelatin capsules). Our integrated capabilities span formulation 
development, analytical services, drug substance and drug product manufacturing, device integration, sterile manufacturing, 
helping customers accelerate development, streamline commercialisation, and scale seamlessly to commercial production.
We operate five state-of-the-art facilities in Bengaluru, India, with regulatory approvals from leading global authorities 
including the US FDA, EMA, MHRA, Health Canada, TGA, WHO GMP, and ANVISA, supported by a workforce of 1,600+ 
professionals. Our diversified customer base spans innovator pharmaceutical companies, global generics manufacturers, 
and biotechnology firms across regulated and international markets. With an integrated, science-led CDMO platform 
and specialised technological capabilities, we are well-positioned to address the evolving requirements of the global 
pharmaceutical industry.
Source: IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2026

Real GDP is estimated to grow to 7.6% in FY26, keeping 
India among the fastest-growing major economies in the 
world, even as geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and 
changing tariff rules made for a tougher global environment. 
Consumer spending continued to be the primary growth 
driver, supported by higher incomes, urbanisation, and 
improving employment trends. Inflation stayed largely within 
the Reserve Bank of India’s target range. To support growth, 
the RBI continued its monetary easing cycle, lowering the 
repo rate to 5.5% in October 2025 and then to 5.25% in 
December 2025. As of February 2026, the RBI maintained 
the repo rate at 5.25% while retaining a neutral policy stance 
amid ongoing global uncertainty.

The global economy is expected to grow at a moderate pace over the medium term. In this volatile environment, 
organisations are expected to keep adjusting how they operate to be more resilient, diversified, and efficient. Supply 
chain security, regional manufacturing, strong partnerships, and the ability to adapt quickly are becoming increasingly 
important to staying competitive. Businesses that can navigate geopolitical complexities, adapt to changing trade 
patterns, and execute with discipline are expected to be better placed to capitalise on emerging opportunities.

Global medicine spending is expected to witness slow growth over the next five years in absolute terms. Most of this growth 
is expected to come from the US, a small group of other high-income, high-growth developed countries, and a set of faster-
growing, lower-income countries known as pharmerging markets, with a handful of these countries accounting for the bulk of 
the increase. In developed markets, growth continues to be driven mainly by the fast adoption of new drugs, most of which 
reach these markets within a year of launch, while growth across pharmerging markets is being driven by improving healthcare

more broadly are expected to keep demand strong for both essential and specialty medicines across markets.

Corporate Overview       Statutory Reports      Financial StatementsIndustry growth is becoming increasingly concentrated 
in a few high-impact therapy areas. According to IQVIA, 
oncology, immunology, and diabetes accounted for 43% of 
global pharmaceutical value in 2025, up 11% since 2019. 
Oncology remained the largest contributor to growth, 
supported by continued innovation and a robust pipeline 
of new therapies. Immunology also continued to be a key 
growth area, driven by the rising prevalence of autoimmune 
and inflammatory diseases and sustained adoption of 
biologic therapies. Within this landscape, obesity emerged 
as one of the fastest-growing therapy areas globally, 
supported by the rapid adoption of GLP-1 therapies.
Growing demand for obesity and metabolic disorder 
treatments continues to support the expansion of the GLP-
1 therapy market. Innovation in both oral and injectable 
therapies, together with a broad development pipeline, is 
contributing to market growth. Additionally, the expiry of 
patents for leading GLP-1 therapies such as semaglutide 
is increasing affordability and access, particularly in price-
sensitive markets, supporting broader patient adoption and 
market expansion.
These market developments are also reshaping the 
pharmaceutical value chain. Higher treatment volumes are 
driving demand for peptide manufacturing, injectable drug 
delivery systems, and sterile manufacturing capabilities. 
Furthermore, the entry of off-patent products and continued 
product innovation are expected to support broader market 
penetration and create additional opportunities across the 
pharmaceutical ecosystem.

and distributionCDMO Industry
Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations 
(CDMOs) have become a critical part of the global 
pharmaceutical ecosystem, as pharmaceutical and 
biotechnology companies increasingly engage specialised 
partners for development and manufacturing. This shift has 
been driven in large part by the growth of biologics, which 
increasingly rely on specialised manufacturing capabilities 
that many pharmaceutical players companies do not have 
in-house. Companies are partnering with CDMOs not just 
to manage overflow capacity, but increasingly as long-term 
strategic partners embedded in their development and 
commercial programmes, helping optimise costs, accelerate 
development timelines, and access specialised capabilities 
without significant capital investment of their own.
The scope of CDMO services has expanded well beyond 
traditional manufacturing to cover the full pharmaceutical 
value chain, including formulation development, analytical 
testing, clinical supply management, and commercial-scale 
production. As companies look for greater efficiency, scale 
and speed-to-market, demand for partners who can support 
the entire journey from development through commercial 
supply continues to grow.
Evolving CDMO Landscape
The global CDMO industry is entering a new phase of sustained 
growth, driven by increasing demand for development 
and manufacturing services, growing drug complexity, 
and a broader shift by pharmaceutical and biotechnology 
companies toward more diversified and resilient supply 
chains.
Much of this growth reflects a broader shift in the kind of 
manufacturing pharmaceutical companies need. While 
small molecule manufacturing continues to account for the 
majority of CDMO demand and remains a stable base for the 
industry, growth is increasingly coming from biologics and 
other complex modalities, including peptides, antibody-drug 
conjugates, and cell and gene therapies, among others.

Pharmaceutical Innovation and Pipeline Growth
Continued advancements in biotechnology and targeted 
therapies are driving growth in pharmaceutical development 
pipelines worldwide. Increased research activity across 
biologics, rare diseases, and specialty therapies is supporting 
demand for outsourced development and manufacturing 
services. As pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies 
seek to accelerate innovation while optimising resources, 
CDMOs continue to play an important role in supporting 
product development and commercialisation.
Expansion of Complex Therapeutics
The growing adoption of biologics, peptides, antibody-
drug conjugates (ADCs), specialty injectables, and 
drug-device combination products is reshaping the 
pharmaceutical landscape. These therapies require 
specialised manufacturing technologies, advanced 
process development capabilities, and stringent regulatory 
oversight, increasing reliance on external development and 
manufacturing partners. The continued growth of GLP-1 
therapies is further supporting demand across sterile fill-
finish operations and drug-delivery systems.Supply Chain Diversification and Resilience
Global pharmaceutical supply chains are evolving as 
companies seek to mitigate geopolitical risks, strengthen 
business continuity, and reduce supply concentration. 
Changing trade dynamics, localisation initiatives, and 
emerging policy measures such as the proposed US 
BIOSECURE Act are encouraging companies to diversify 
manufacturing and sourcing strategies. These trends 
are creating opportunities for CDMOs with scalable 
infrastructure, strong quality systems, and a track record 
of reliable execution.
Shift Towards Integrated CDMO Partnerships
The industry is increasingly moving beyond traditional 
outsourcing arrangements toward integrated 
partnerships spanning development, manufacturing, 
and commercialisation. Pharmaceutical companies are 
consolidating supplier networks and partnering with service 
providers capable of offering end-to-end solutions. This 
trend is supporting the growth of integrated CDMO models 
by improving coordination, reducing development timelines, 
and enhancing operational efficiency.These therapies demand advanced technical expertise 
and infrastructure that few companies choose to build 
internally, encouraging greater reliance on CDMO partners. 
Biologics-focused CDMOs have become a core part of the 
pharmaceutical industry, providing end-to-end support 
from early-stage development through to commercial-
scale manufacturing, and are increasingly seen as strategic 
partners in the biologics sector.
Alongside this shift, rising global demand for GLP-1 and 
other weight-loss therapies is driving strong investment into 
CDMO capacity built specifically to support this category, 
from peptide manufacturing to the devices used to deliver 
these drugs, such as pens and auto-injectors. This has made 
GLP-1s one of the industry’s most significant near-term 
growth drivers, with pharmaceutical companies increasingly 
relying on CDMO partners that can scale production quickly 
to keep up with demand.Outlook
The CDMO industry is expected to maintain strong

Drug-Device Combination (including GLP-1s)
The DDC segment is emerging as one of the fastest-
growing areas within the pharmaceutical industry, with the 
global CDMO market for DDCs, including GLP-1 therapies, 
expected to grow at a CAGR of over 20%. Pharmaceutical 
companies are increasingly adopting delivery formats such 
as autoinjectors, cartridge-based platforms to improve 
patient convenience, treatment adherence, and product 
differentiation. This trend is driving demand for specialised 
formulation development, device integration, sterile fill-

key growth driver has been the rapid expansion of GLP-
1 therapies for obesity and metabolic disorders, which 
has accelerated investments across the broader delivery 
ecosystem, including peptide manufacturing, sterile fill-

assembly. Beyond GLP-1 therapies, the increasing adoption 
of injectable biologics and other specialty therapies

In an increasingly competitive pharmaceutical environment, 
speed-to-market has become an important strategic priority. 
Pharmaceutical companies are seeking partners that can 
accelerate development timelines, facilitate technology 
transfer, and support rapid commercial scale-up. At the same 
time, digital technologies and automation are improving 
manufacturing efficiency, quality management, and supply chain planning through enhanced process monitoring and 
data-driven decision-making. Customers are also placing 
greater emphasis on manufacturing readiness, favouring 
partners with established facilities, proven regulatory 
compliance, and strong technical capabilities that can 
support efficient execution and timely product launches.

Biologics (Drug Substance and Drug Product)
Biologics continue to be one of the fastest-growing segments 
within the pharmaceutical industry, with the biologics CDMO 
market for drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) 
expected to grow at a CAGR of around 14% over the medium 
term. Growth is being driven by increasing investment in 
biologics research and development, rising adoption across 
a broad range of therapeutic areas, and continued demand 
from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies for 
specialised development and manufacturing capabilities.
The market continues to benefit from a strong innovation 
pipeline and growing biosimilar adoption. As several leading 
biologics lose patent exclusivity, biosimilar development 
activity is accelerating, supported by favourable regulatory 
pathways, increasing healthcare cost pressures, and efforts 
to expand patient access. At the same time, the biologics 
pipeline remains robust, encompassing monoclonal 
antibodies, recombinant proteins, cell and gene therapies, 
and other emerging modalities. India is also emerging as 
a key hub for biologics development and manufacturing, 
supported by a skilled talent pool, cost competitiveness, and 
expanding industry capabilities. The increasing complexity 
of these products, together with the need for specialised 
development and manufacturing expertise, is driving 
continued demand for CDMO services across the biologics 
value chain.As a result, CDMOs with capabilities spanning biologics 
development, process optimisation, analytical services, 
and commercial-scale manufacturing are well positioned 
to benefit from growing demand. Pharmaceutical and 
biotechnology companies are increasingly seeking partners 
with integrated capabilities, technical expertise and 
proven quality systems to support the development and 
commercialisation of complex biologic therapies.
Softgel Capsules1

steady growth, with the global softgel capsules market 
expected to grow at a CAGR of around 9% over the medium

in pharmaceutical-grade softgels, high technical skill 
requirements, and specialised manufacturing capabilities, 
and increasing demand for CDMO services. Continued 
product innovation and lifecycle extension opportunities 
are also supporting demand for specialised softgel 
manufacturing.

Operational Performance in FY26
FY26 marked a year of continued capability building and 
commercial progress, strengthening the foundation for 
sustainable long-term growth across our specialty platforms. 
Commercial momentum remained strong across service 
offerings supported by a growing commercial pipeline 
and expanding engagement with existing customers. The 
year witnessed significant progress across our key growth 
platforms. We strengthened our position in GLP-1s by 
securing the first three generic semaglutide approvals in G7 
markets, two approvals in Canada and one in the US through 
our partners, while enabling multiple Day-1 launches in India 
across a diversified customer base. We also completed 
multiple Tirzepatide NCE-1 filings for our customers, further 
expanding our participation in the obesity and metabolic 
therapies segment. Our biologics business continued to gain 
momentum, with the opportunity funnel expanding nearly 4x 
over FY25, supported by the addition of a European biosimilar partner, a major US biosimilar customer and a second project 
from a leading global animal health company. Across our 
injectables and softgel businesses, we signed multiple 
licensing and CDMO agreements, launched new products and 
further expanded our customer base and specialty product 
portfolio.
We continued to invest in manufacturing infrastructure, 
talent and operational capabilities to support future 
growth. Capacity expansion programmes remained on 
track, supporting our preparedness for future commercial 
opportunities. During the year, we successfully completed 
49 regulatory inspections and customer audits, including 
USFDA and EMA inspections, reinforcing our commitment to 
quality and compliance. Supported by a growing commercial 
pipeline, expanding biologics opportunities and continued 
progress across complex modalities, we remain well 
positioned to support the next phase of growth across our 
integrated CDMO platform.

Risk Management
We follow a structured and integrated approach to risk 
management, designed to anticipate, assess and mitigate 
risks in a timely and effective manner. In an increasingly dynamic global environment characterised by evolving 
regulatory requirements, supply chain complexities, 
geopolitical developments, and market uncertainties, 
proactive risk management remains fundamental to 
sustaining our growth, operational resilience, and long-term 
value creation.
Our risk management framework enables the continuous 
identification, assessment and monitoring of strategic, 
operational, financial and compliance risks, ensuring 
appropriate mitigation measures are embedded across 
the organisation. We regularly evaluate both existing and 
emerging risks, strengthen internal controls and governance 
mechanisms, and implement targeted action plans to 
safeguard business continuity, protect stakeholder interests 
and support the consistent execution of our strategic 
priorities.
For more details, refer to the ‘Risk Management’ section on 
page 116 of this report.
Internal Audit Systems and Their Adequacy
We maintain a robust internal control framework tailored 
to the scope and complexity of our operations. Detailed 
policies and procedures cover financial, operational, and 
compliance domains, ensuring disciplined execution and 
responsibility. Supported by capable professionals and a 
continuous internal audit programme, we regularly assess 
control adequacy and suggest process, policy, accounting, 
and regulatory enhancements. Internal Auditors work closely 
with Senior Management to keep our controls dynamic and 
adaptable. The Audit Committee further enhances oversight 
by reviewing audit findings and ensuring improvements are 
implemented.

6. Update on Corporate Actions
  During the year under review and to the date of this 
Report, your Company has undertaken/ initiated the 
following key corporate actions:
 Scheme of Arrangements
6.1  Scheme of Arrangement for acquisition of 
European CDMO business of SteriScience 
and anti-infective business from Brooks 
SteriScience.
  The Board of Directors at their meeting held on 
September 26, 2025, approved a strategic transaction 
to strengthen the company’s capabilities and 
capacity by acquiring the European CDMO business of 
Steriscience and anti-infective business from Brooks 
Steriscience.
  The said transaction was intended to be achieved 
through a Scheme of Amalgamation amongst 
Steriscience Specialties Private Limited, Brooks 
Steriscience Limited, Steriscience Pte. Limited, Strides 
Pharma Services Private Limited and OneSource 
Specialty Pharma Limited and their respective 
shareholders (under section 230 to 232 read with 
section 234, section 52, section 66 of the Act and under section 210 read with section 212 of The Singapore 
Companies Act, 1967 and other applicable provisions 
of the Act, the Singapore Companies Act, 1967 and the 
rules framed thereunder).
  The National Stock Exchange of India Limited and  
BSE Limited by their respective letters dated  
February 25, 2026 conveyed their “No-objection /No 
Adverse Observation Letter”, for the Scheme.
  However, the Board of Directors at their meeting held 
on May 13, 2026, in the best interest of stakeholders 
decided to not pursue the transaction in the current 
form and revisit it following successful delivery of 
respective companies’ FY28 guidance.
6.2  Amalgamation of Stelis Pte. Limited with 
OneSource Specialty Pte. Limited, wholly 
owned subsidiaries of OneSource Specialty 
Pharma Limited (“the Company”)
  Stelis Pte. Limited (“Stelis”), Singapore a wholly 
owned subsidiary of the Company amalgamated 
with OneSource Specialty Pte. Limited (“OneSource 
Specialty Pte.”), Singapore another wholly owned 
subsidiary of the Company with effect from  
January 01, 2026 to simplify the existing corporate 
hierarchy, enhance operational efficiency, and eliminate 
redundant administrative, compliance, and legal costs.
  Since the transaction was undertaken between the 
wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company, there is no 
impact on a consolidated basis and on the shareholding 
pattern of the Company.
6.3  Striking off of the wholly owned subsidiary 
entity – Stelis Biopharma UK Private Limited
  Stelis Biopharma UK Private Limited was struck off with 
effect from October 14, 2025, as there was no business 
activity and remained dormant since its incorporation 
on November 30, 2022.
